name: Li Ling
bio: Li Ling (李陵, style name Shaoqing) was a general of the Western Han dynasty, grandson of the famous commander Li Guang. In 99 BC he led a small infantry force against the Xiongnu, was surrounded and, after resisting to the end, surrendered. Emperor Wu, enraged, had his family put to death, and Li Ling remained among the Xiongnu until his death in 74 BC. His birth year is not recorded; c. 134 BC is an approximation.

Three five-character poems addressed to his friend Su Wu, who had been held captive by the Xiongnu and was allowed to return home, are preserved in the Wenxuan (Selections of Refined Literature), together with a letter. The attribution of these poems to Li Ling is traditional and has long been doubted; many scholars regard them as later compositions in the style of the anonymous Han poems, so they are given here under his name on the authority of the anthology only. The text is taken from the Wikisource edition of Wenxuan with Li Shan's commentary, with the commentary and collation notes removed.

poems.title: 與蘇武 其一 (Yu Su Wu qi yi)
poems.author: Li Ling
poems.text:
良時不再至
離別在須臾
屏營衢路側
執手野踟躕
仰視浮雲馳
奄忽互相踰
風波一失所
各在天一隅
長當從此別
且復立斯須
欲因晨風發
送子以賤軀

poems.title: 與蘇武 其二 (Yu Su Wu qi er)
poems.author: Li Ling
poems.text:
嘉會難再遇
三載為千秋
臨河濯長纓
念子悵悠悠
遠望悲風至
對酒不能酬
行人懷往路
何以慰我愁
獨有盈觴酒
與子結綢繆

poems.title: 與蘇武 其三 (Yu Su Wu qi san)
poems.author: Li Ling
poems.text:
攜手上河梁
遊子暮何之
徘徊蹊路側
悢悢不得辭
行人難久留
各言長相思
安知非日月
弦望自有時
努力崇明德
皓首以為期
